page: Amazon Web Services g5.12xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R32 processor featuring 24 physical cores and 48 virtual CPUs running at 3.3 GHz across an x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is configured at 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, offering a 4.0 GB allocation per core. The instance includes 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 40 Gbps.

Hardware acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPUs providing a combined total of 89 GB of video memory. In synthetic testing, this multi-GPU configuration achieves top-tier results in large language model inference, delivering 2,835.71 tokens per second during prompt processing for 7B models and sustaining 397.97 tokens per second for 70B models. Text generation benchmarks also score in the upper quartiles across small, medium, and large model architectures. PassMark encryption tests and memory bandwidth benchmarks show strong performance in the upper 25 percent tier.

The CPU subsystem exhibits moderate performance, with stress-ng single-core execution scoring in the bottom decile while multi-core workloads, Geekbench runs, and PassMark CPU metrics align with mid-range baselines. Single-thread processing bottlenecks can emerge if workloads are heavily CPU-bound rather than offloaded to the GPU accelerators. Storage and networking performance remain steady, supporting multi-gigabyte compression, sustained static web throughput, and stable Redis transactional rates.

Amazon Web Services g5.12xlarge provides balanced resource density by pairing quad enterprise GPUs with substantial local NVMe disk and high network throughput. It is specifically suited for machine learning inference, model fine-tuning, multi-stream video transcoding, 3D graphics rendering, and data pipeline processing where high GPU memory and rapid local disk access are essential.
description: Amazon Web Services g5.12xlarge is an accelerated computing instance equipped with 48 vCPUs from a dedicated 24-core AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The host includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 40 Gbps baseline networking. Acceleration is provided by four NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPUs with 89 GB of aggregate VRAM. Benchmark results show top-decile throughput in LLM prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large parameter models, paired with strong cryptographic and memory bandwidth figures. While general-purpose CPU scores remain in average ranges, the dense GPU and NVMe allocation yields balanced cost efficiency for acceleration-heavy tasks. The instance is well matched for deep learning inference, distributed graphics rendering, spatial computing, and high-throughput video processing workloads.
